name: Rishi Singh
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Harness; founder & CEO, SapientAI / BaseRock.ai (AI software testing)
profile: IIT Delhi-trained engineer who spent five years at Apple leading its deployment-automation platform, then co-founded Harness (AI software delivery platform) with Jyoti Bansal and served as CTO until 2021. He remains on Harness's board and now runs an AI test-generation startup (SapientAI, launched May 2023 with $5M seed from 8VC; BaseRock.ai).
interesting_fact: SapientAI emerged from stealth in May 2023 with a $5M seed led by 8VC to build an 'AI Test Coder' that writes unit tests automatically.
deep_cut_fact: Before Harness he spent five years at Apple leading development of its internal deployment automation platform, and says he learned from Steve Jobs the importance of constantly talking about what you believe in.
notes: Not the founder-CEO of Harness (that is Jyoti Bansal); he is the technical co-founder. Best route likely via his current AI-testing startup.

name: Garrett Lord
profile: Michigan native who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, in 2014 with Michigan Tech classmates Ben Christensen and Scott Ringwelski, leaving school a few credits short to raise capital. Handshake was valued at $3.5B (Series F, 2022). Since late 2024 he has pushed a 'refounding' via Handshake AI, which recruits domain experts to train AI models.
interesting_fact: He conceived Handshake AI at the company's 2024 Christmas party; the unit was projected to hit about $100M in annual recurring revenue, and he calls the pivot the 'refounding of Handshake'.
deep_cut_fact: At Michigan Tech he worked as a ski patroller at Mont Ripley, played broomball, and scavenged campus dumpsters for parts for his IT side business; he also cold-emailed recruiters to land a Palantir internship and won its summer hackathon.

public_contacts.value: Notion 'First Block' interview with Garrett Lord

notes: Very accessible founder with lots of interviews; Handshake AI (data-for-AI) angle relevant to a data-center/AI podcast.

name: Laura Spiekerman
current_role: Co-founder & President, Alloy (identity and fraud prevention platform)
profile: Fintech operator who co-founded Alloy in 2015 with Tommy Nicholas and Charles Hearn after the three met at an ACH payments startup. Alloy provides identity verification, KYC/AML and fraud-prevention tooling to 900+ banks, credit unions and fintechs and was valued at about $1.55B in 2021. She serves as President and leads go-to-market and partnerships.
interesting_fact: Alloy's platform is used by over 900 banks, credit unions and fintechs to manage identity, KYC/AML compliance and fraud risk.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alloy she was the first hire at Kenyan payments company Kopo Kopo, where watching M-Pesa 'change people's financial lives' drew her to financial infrastructure.
notes: Some profiles list her as CRO or COO; Alloy's own site says President. Frequent fintech conference speaker.

name: Sujay Tyle
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Merama (Latin American e-commerce brand builder/aggregator)
profile: US-born serial founder who entered Harvard at 15, left as a 2011 Thiel Fellow, and worked at Scopely before moving to Berlin to co-found Frontier Car Group (emerging-market used-car marketplaces), acquired by OLX/Naspers in 2019. He then co-founded Merama, which acquires and scales consumer brands selling on Mercado Libre and Amazon across Latin America, reaching unicorn status.
interesting_fact: He was a freshman at Harvard by age 15 and left in his junior year to become one of Peter Thiel's original '20 Under 20' fellows.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008, as a teenager, he co-founded ReSight with his older brother Sheel, a venture aimed at democratizing eye-care services.
notes: No published personal/press contact found; Merama's website has no press email. Route via Merama or Frontier Car Group investors.

name: Rob Forman
current_role: CEO coach (listed with Scalebound); independent board member (e.g., Grayscale); co-founder & former President, Salesloft
profile: Atlanta software engineer-turned-founder who co-founded Salesloft, the sales engagement platform, serving as head of technology and later President & Chief Strategy Officer. Vista Equity Partners acquired Salesloft in December 2021 for $2.3B. He now coaches CEOs on organizational health and execution and sits on company boards.
interesting_fact: Salesloft, which he co-founded and served as President, was acquired by Vista Equity Partners in December 2021 for $2.3B.
deep_cut_fact: Before Salesloft he co-founded HireIQ, a call-center hiring and machine-learning analytics company, serving as its CTO; it was later acquired by Verint Systems.
notes: Faith-driven entrepreneur active in the Praxis network; LinkedIn is the best published route. Board roles (Grayscale, Hubstaff) per aggregators, unverified on primary sources.

name: Eyal Goren
current_role: Co-founder of Fabric (formerly CommonSense Robotics); reportedly no longer at the company, founder of AutoBirds (AI/MVP studio, Israel) per aggregator profile
profile: Israeli engineer who in 2015 co-founded CommonSense Robotics (later Fabric) with his brother Elram Goren (CEO), Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen, building robotic micro-fulfillment centers for grocery and retail e-commerce. Fabric raised $200M in 2021 at a $1B+ valuation. Eyal held software, business development and strategic partnerships roles and is a named co-inventor on Fabric patents.
interesting_fact: Fabric's 2021 $200M Series C made it what the company billed a 'robocorn' - a robotics unicorn built on small urban micro-fulfillment sites.
deep_cut_fact: Fabric (then CommonSense Robotics) was founded in 2015 by two brothers, Elram and Eyal Goren, together with Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen.
notes: Low public profile; the CEO and public face of Fabric is his brother Elram Goren. Current role (AutoBirds) only from an aggregator; verify on LinkedIn. No published contact found.

name: Matthew Gross
current_role: Founder & Executive Chair, Newsela (title per recent profiles; verify)
profile: Former Teach for America music teacher and New York education-policy leader who founded Newsela in 2013, an edtech platform that adapts news and instructional texts to each student's reading level. Newsela raised $100M in 2021 at a $1B valuation and later combined with Formative; Gross moved from CEO to executive chair.
interesting_fact: He started Newsela after a meeting with his struggling-reader son's assistant principal left him feeling the school had given up on his son.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a Teach for America corps member teaching music at C.S. 50 in the South Bronx, and before Newsela ran the Regents Research Fund, which helped implement New York's Race to the Top reforms. His favorite school subject: U.S. History.
notes: Exact current title unclear (sources differ between executive chair and co-founder after CEO change). Also on New Classrooms board.

name: Fred Helou
current_role: Founder & CEO, Vagaro (salon, spa and fitness booking/business software)
profile: Lebanese-American software engineer (Fady 'Fred' Helou) who fled Beirut during the civil war, rose to software director at Novellus, and after being laid off in the Great Recession founded Vagaro in 2009 in the Bay Area. Vagaro provides booking, payments and marketing software for beauty, wellness and fitness businesses and reached a $1B valuation after an FTV Capital investment.
interesting_fact: The idea for Vagaro came on a business trip to South Korea, when he wanted to book a haircut with his American barber online and found no way to do it.
deep_cut_fact: He left Beirut at 19, was pickpocketed of all his savings during an airport layover, and started in the U.S. on a $5-an-hour delivery job while attending school full-time; in Vagaro's early days he personally handled customer support.

public_contacts.value: Vagaro 'On Point' podcast episode with Fred Helou

notes: Openly shares immigrant-founder story; Fast Company Executive Board member. No published press email found; route via Vagaro corporate communications.

name: Kari Kivela
current_role: Co-founder of Oura Health (former CTO & Head of Design); current role at Oura unverified
profile: Finnish engineer-designer (Kari Kivelä) who co-founded Oura in Oulu in 2013 with Petteri Lahtela and Markku Koskela, drawing on the region's Polar/Nokia hardware heritage. As early CTO and head of design he shaped the smart ring that measures sleep and recovery; Oura has since grown into a multi-billion-dollar wearable company (valued around $11B in 2025).
interesting_fact: Oura's 2015 Kickstarter hit its $100,000 goal in 15 hours and gathered about $650,000 in pre-orders with no PR or paid ads.
deep_cut_fact: Oura was originally called 'Jouzen' - from joutsen, Finnish for swan, plus 'Zen'. Kivelä's design credo: 'design shouldn't be dictated by technology,' calling miniaturizing the electronics the biggest challenge.
notes: Low public profile; Oura's public face is CEO Tom Hale. Deep-cut combines two sources: Jouzen name from ouraring.com history blog, quote from Fashnerd. Only route found is Oura company press email.

name: Igor Teleshevsky
current_role: Co-founder of Capitolis; EVP & Head of Professional Services as of 2020 (current role unverified)
profile: Israeli capital-markets technologist who co-founded Capitolis in 2017 with Gil Mandelzis (CEO) and led its engineering until 2020, then became EVP and Head of Professional Services, relocating to New York. Capitolis builds platforms for banks to optimize capital and portfolios and was valued around $2B+ in 2022. Earlier he spent ~15 years at post-trade firm Traiana (ICAP).
interesting_fact: As co-founder he built and led Capitolis's engineering from its 2017 founding - the platform the company says is 'reimagining how global capital markets operate' for banks and asset managers.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 he handed the engineering leadership he had held since founding to Amos Arev and moved from Tel Aviv to Capitolis's New York office to run client onboarding and success.
notes: Behind-the-scenes co-founder; earlier career (Traiana EVP Engineering & GM Israel, Hebrew University CS) from aggregator Zippia, unverified. One source lists him as former co-founder, so he may have left.

name: Kevin Bennett
current_role: Former CEO of Caribou (auto refinance fintech, formerly MotoRefi); reportedly left in Sept 2023 and has since started new fintech/proptech ventures (unverified)
profile: Washington, DC-area serial entrepreneur who led MotoRefi, incubated by QED Investors in 2016, as CEO from 2018 and rebranded it Caribou in 2021 as it expanded from auto refinancing into auto insurance; the company reached a $1B+ valuation. He reportedly stepped down as CEO in 2023 and has been building new startups since.
interesting_fact: He has said Caribou was the fifth startup he worked on, pitching it as a 'mission-driven fintech' to help the American middle class save on a $1.4 trillion auto-debt market long untouched by digital innovation.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining the 2021 rebrand from MotoRefi to Caribou on a December podcast, he noted that caribou are also called reindeer - 'seasonally appropriate.'

public_contacts.value: Fintech One-on-One podcast #335 with Kevin Bennett

notes: Sources differ on whether he was a founder or joined as CEO in 2018. Post-Caribou ventures (Homezen, Further) only from secondary sources; confirm via LinkedIn.

name: Francisco Hein
current_role: Co-founder & CMO, Fever (live-entertainment discovery and ticketing platform); behind Secret Media Network
profile: Marketer-entrepreneur who co-founded Fever in 2014 with CEO Ignacio Bachiller and Alexandre Pérez Casares after helping launch dating app Happn. Fever, based in Madrid and New York, powers experiences such as Candlelight concerts and runs the Secret Media Network (Secret London, Secret NYC, etc.) to drive demand; it has raised over $500M and is valued above $2B.
interesting_fact: Besides Fever, he is listed as founder of Secret Media Network, the city-guide publisher (Secret London, Secret NYC and others) that sits alongside Fever's ticketing business; at Fever he started as co-founder in charge of growth.
deep_cut_fact: Before Fever he was on the founding team of dating app Happn, leading its user acquisition and expansion; he studied business in Paris, Shanghai and New York and sits on Meta's EMEA Advisory Board.
notes: No published personal or press email found; Fever's public face is CEO Ignacio Bachiller. Current exact title (CMO) from job listings/theorg; verify.

name: Amit Bareket
current_role: Co-founder & former CEO, Perimeter 81 (acquired by Check Point); reportedly VP of SASE at Check Point Software (verify)
profile: Israeli cybersecurity entrepreneur and IDF Unit 81 veteran who, after engineering stints at IBM XIV Storage and BigBand Networks, co-founded consumer VPN SaferVPN with Sagi Gidali (sold to J2 Global) and then Perimeter 81, a cloud network-security/SASE platform. Check Point agreed to acquire Perimeter 81 for about $490M in August 2023, after it had been valued at $1B in 2022.
interesting_fact: Perimeter 81 is named after IDF Unit 81, the elite technology intelligence unit Bareket served in; co-founder Sagi Gidali came from Unit 9900.
deep_cut_fact: He holds eight patents covering storage, mobile applications and UI, graduated cum laude in Computer Science and Economics from Tel Aviv University, and his company bio jokes he has 'a poker face that's great for keeping secrets or for deadpan humor.'
notes: Contributor to SC World and Forbes Technology Council. No published press email; route via Check Point media relations.

name: Tommy Ricketts
current_role: CEO & Co-founder, BeZero Carbon (carbon credit ratings agency, London)
profile: Former political strategist (London, Brussels) and Bank of America global research VP who co-founded BeZero Carbon with Sebastien Cross in 2020. BeZero rates the quality of carbon credits for buyers, investors and developers, raised a $50M Series B, and has applied for ESMA recognition as a ratings provider.
interesting_fact: BeZero publishes its headline carbon-credit ratings openly, arguing that not every credit really equals a tonne of CO2 avoided or removed.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, the day he turned 18, was as a barman at his local pub; he broke into the City by texting his old politics boss 'Can I come with you?' and spent the Brexit referendum night writing his bank's response.
notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast guest (Modo Energy Transmission, Burns Sheehan). Strong fit for an energy/climate podcast.

name: Bernat Farrero
current_role: Co-founder of Factorial (HR software; listed as CRO/executive); Co-CEO & founder of Itnig (Barcelona startup ecosystem and fund)
profile: Barcelona engineer (UPC, PoliTo) who founded Itnig in 2010 as a development consultancy and turned it into a startup studio that spawned about a dozen companies, including Camaloon, Quipu (exited to Providence) and Parkimeter. In 2016 he co-founded Factorial with Jordi Romero and Pau Ramon; the HR software company became a unicorn in 2022.
interesting_fact: Itnig began in 2010 literally in a family garage in Barcelona, and almost from day one ran its own tech podcast - its first product, Camaloon, sold over €200,000 of custom magnets and badges in its first months.
deep_cut_fact: Itnig's 2012 'Hacker Accelerator' launched Playfulbet, which reached 1,000 users in 22 days; Farrero describes the early Itnig team as 'nerds' always looking for excuses to sell projects and try new things.
notes: Exact Factorial title varies by source (CEO & CRO / co-founder). Itnig podcast is a natural peer-to-peer outreach route. Deep-cut combines both Itnig pages (Playfulbet stat on /about).

name: Joshua Weiss
current_role: Co-founder, First Mode (hydrogen/hybrid mining-truck decarbonization; assets acquired by Cummins in 2025); current role unknown
profile: Josh Weiss is listed among the 11 founders of First Mode, started in Seattle in March 2018 by former members of asteroid-mining company Planetary Resources. First Mode built hybrid battery and hydrogen fuel-cell powertrains for mining haul trucks and rail; Anglo American became majority owner in a 2023 $200M deal, and Cummins acquired First Mode's assets in 2025.
interesting_fact: First Mode and Anglo American debuted the world's largest hydrogen-powered mine haul truck (a converted Komatsu 930E) in 2022 at the Mogalakwena platinum mine in South Africa.
deep_cut_fact: First Mode was founded on March 14, 2018 by 11 alumni of asteroid-mining startup Planetary Resources, including Josh Weiss - space-hardware engineers who pivoted to decarbonizing mining.
notes: Limited research: web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so only Wikipedia was checked. Wikipedia lists 'Josh Weiss' as one of 11 founders, but his individual role and whereabouts are unverified. Company website blocks scripted access. Highly relevant to energy podcast if reachable.

name: You Zheng
current_role: Former Dongfeng Motor Group Party Standing Committee member & deputy general manager who launched Voyah (岚图) in 2020; current role unverified
profile: You Zheng (尤峥) was the senior Dongfeng Motor executive who unveiled Voyah, Dongfeng's premium EV brand, in Wuhan in July 2020 and introduced its management team (CEO/CTO Lu Fang). Voyah is a state-controlled Dongfeng subsidiary (Dongfeng holds ~79%) now listed in Hong Kong; he is a state-enterprise executive rather than an owner-founder.
interesting_fact: At Voyah's 2020 launch he pitched it as a 'new force in Chinese car-making' using new organization, mechanisms and business model to offer 'zero-anxiety' premium smart EVs; the name 岚图 puns on 蓝图 ('blueprint').
deep_cut_fact: Voyah's logo, unveiled by You Zheng in July 2020 at Wuhan's Big House contemporary art center, draws on the kun-peng spreading its wings from the Zhuangzi chapter 'Free and Easy Wandering'.
notes: Likely a data-quality issue: he is a state-owned-enterprise manager, not a wealthy founder, so probably not a UHNW individual. Web search quota ran out; only the CAAM 2020 article and Wikipedia were checked. Voyah is led by Lu Fang (Chairman & CEO). Unlikely podcast target.

name: Michael E. Mendelsohn
current_role: Founder & Chief Strategy Officer, Cardurion Pharmaceuticals (Burlington, MA)
profile: Harvard-trained cardiologist and physician-scientist who led cardiovascular research at Tufts (1993-2010) and Merck Research Laboratories (SVP and global head, 2010-13), then became a venture partner at SV Life Sciences and in 2016 founded Cardurion, which develops heart-failure drugs and has operations in the US and Japan. He was executive chairman before becoming Chief Strategy Officer.
interesting_fact: At Merck (2010-2013) he was global head of cardiovascular research, overseeing everything from drug discovery to late-stage development.
deep_cut_fact: He studied both chemistry and English at Amherst College, and at Tufts founded the Molecular Cardiology Research Institute and became the medical center's first-ever chief scientific officer.

public_contacts.value: info@cardurion.com (listed for media and general inquiries)

notes: Not to be confused with film financier Michael Mendelsohn (Patriot Pictures). Biotech, so limited fit with energy/data-center themes.
